note: Pins the two copies of the shared kernel (ADR 0001, docs/adr/0001-standalone-engine.md). tests/test_kernel_sync.py fails when either copy changes.
known_differences: util.py, provenance.py, lock.py: the copies run the same logic (tests/test_kernel_sync.py compares their syntax trees with every string masked). They differ only in the words of messages and docstrings (vpg/pdg, production/project, .vpg/.pdg, N23) and in pdg's BRIEF_PLACEHOLDER constant (pdg_only). Re-compared 2026-09-27 after vpg v1.1 added is_human_name (case-insensitive agent/dry-run check); ported to pdg, where memory.is_human also requires the project's humans list. Re-compared 2026-10-04 after vpg v1.7 added Ledger.stamp (a dict merged into every event while set, never over an event's own fields); ported to pdg with a test (tests/test_hardening.py).

Both ledgers write ahead and are anchored to the saved state (deferred, write_lines, recover, pending_fill, reaches), raise LedgerCorrupt or LedgerBehind on a damaged or lagging ledger, refuse a concurrent change (ConcurrentChange, file_identity) and open only regular files (NotRegularFile, open_regular, open_append, _regular_or_absent).

Engine side (not pinned, see docs/state-model.md): both engines record ledger_tail on every save, keep a human action's events in pending_ledger until they are written, and let only a named human accept a ledger break. pdg additionally protects node commits with its commit journal.
Paths: vpg keeps run state in .vpg/, pdg in .pdg/.
When the kernel is extracted (ADR 0001 trigger), either copy is a valid starting point; the logic check proves they match.
